The question

What if returning to interrupted work felt less like starting over? ReEntry is a calm browser task agent that notices unfinished work, preserves progress, and helps users return to the right next step.

Designing for recovery

The project combines a browser companion with a web application. It keeps live tasks and next actions prominent, with evidence, corrections, and history available when needed.

  • Checkpoint editing, ten-revision history, and restore preserve a path back when work changes.
  • Draft recovery and conflict protection handle interrupted editing and competing updates.
  • Evidence-linked progress distinguishes tentative research, validation, and completion.
  • A provider-independent harness supports local Ollama models or NVIDIA-hosted inference, with separate consent for processing.

THE RECOVERY LOOP

Observe with permission→Preserve evidence→Suggest next step→Review & resume
Users can inspect, correct, restore, and remove captured work. Hosted processing requires explicit agreement.

What exists today

The core recovery journey, history, draft recovery, and automatic-agent preview are implemented. The repository includes automated accessibility and browser checks, evaluation material, and real-model demonstration recordings.

This is a technical preview. Native VoiceOver and manual zoom/text-setting acceptance remain pending, and the recorded demonstrations don’t establish accuracy across arbitrary websites. The project’s documentation records the current verification limits.

Why this work interests me

It brings product design, browser integration, AI inference, and recoverable state into the same problem. Making the system understandable—and giving people a way to correct it—is part of the engineering.
